biological.citation: CaMK4: Structure, physiological functions, and therapeutic potential (PMID: 38615920)
biological.summary: CaMK4 is a versatile serine/threonine kinase that regulates T-cell differentiation, podocyte function, tumor cell proliferation/apoptosis, β cell mass, and insulin sensitivity. It is a key component of Ca2+-activated signaling pathways and acts by phosphorylating downstream target proteins to regulate cellular signaling. The review highlights its structural motifs, activation mechanisms, and potential as a therapeutic target in multiple diseases.

biological.citation: Calcium/calmodulin-dependent protein kinase IV promotes imiquimod-induced psoriatic inflammation via macrophages and keratinocytes in mice (PMID: 35869084)
biological.summary: CaMK4 expression is significantly increased in psoriatic lesional skin from patients and in an IMQ-induced mouse model. In macrophages, CaMK4 inhibits IL-10 production, promoting excessive inflammation; Camk4-/- mice show reduced psoriasis severity. In keratinocytes, CaMK4 inhibits apoptosis, promotes proliferation, and drives expression of pro-inflammatory genes S100A8 and CAMP.

biological.citation: CaMK4 controls follicular helper T cell expansion and function during normal and autoimmune T-dependent B cell responses (PMID: 38287012)
biological.summary: CaMK4 promotes T follicular helper (Tfh) cell expansion by controlling the Tfh-specific transcription factor BCL6 at the transcriptional level through CREMα. In the absence of CaMK4 in T cells, germinal center formation and humoral immunity are impaired, reducing anti-dsDNA titres and kidney IgG/complement deposition in lupus-prone mice. In human Tfh cells, CaMK4 inhibition reduced BCL6 expression and IL-21 secretion, impairing plasmablast formation and IgG production.

biological.citation: CaMK4 compromises podocyte function in autoimmune and nonautoimmune kidney disease (PMID: 29985166)
biological.summary: CaMK4 is overexpressed in podocytes from patients with lupus nephritis and focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, and in lupus-prone and LPS- or adriamycin-treated mice. CaMK4 modulates podocyte motility by altering GTPases Rac1 and RhoA expression, suppresses nephrin and synaptopodin expression, and phosphorylates scaffold protein 14-3-3β leading to synaptopodin degradation. Targeted delivery of a CaMK4 inhibitor to podocytes preserved ultrastructure and suppressed proteinuria in multiple mouse models.

biological.citation: TIPRL Regulates Stemness and Survival in Lung Cancer Stem Cells through CaMKK2-CaMK4-CREB Feedback Loop Activation (PMID: 39076120)
biological.summary: In lung cancer stem cells, TIPRL binds CaMKK2 to sustain its activation, which in turn activates CaMK4, leading to phosphorylation of CREB at Ser129 and Ser133 and constitutive expression of Bcl2 and HMG20A. CREB also activates TIPRL transcription, forming a positive feedback loop (CREB-TIPRL-CaMKK2-CaMK4-CREB) that drives stemness and survival. TIPRL depletion sensitized lung cancer stem cells to afatinib-induced death and reduced metastasis in vivo.

biological.citation: CAMKK2-CAMK4 signaling regulates transferrin trafficking, turnover, and iron homeostasis (PMID: 32460794)
biological.summary: Loss of CAMK4 in mice leads to abnormal post-translational modifications and turnover of transferrin in cerebellum and liver, associated with iron dyshomeostasis. In CRISPR/Cas9-deleted HEK293 cells, absence of CAMKK2-CAMK4 signaling altered intracellular Ca2+ homeostasis and disrupted receptor-mediated transferrin trafficking and TF-receptor protein complex interactions. This study establishes a mechanistic link between CAMKK2-CAMK4 signaling, intracellular Ca2+ levels, and iron homeostasis.

biological.citation: CaMK modulates sensory neural activity to control longevity and proteostasis (PMID: 40359038)
biological.summary: Reduced CaMK4 expression in the human frontal cortex correlates with longevity. In C. elegans, loss of the CaMK4 homolog CMK-1 increases lifespan and enhances proteostasis, primarily through suppressed excitation in AFD thermosensory neurons. This suppression promotes INS-1/insulin release from AIZ neurons, activating DAF-16/FOXO in the intestine, revealing a conserved mechanism by which CaMK regulates lifespan through sensory neural activity.

biological.citation: Convergence on CaMK4: A Key Modulator of Autism-Associated Signaling Pathways in Neurons (PMID: 39442785)
biological.summary: CAMK4 is identified as an emerging risk gene for autism spectrum disorder (ASD), with 3 likely pathogenic variants with monogenic effect found in individuals with hyperkinetic movement disorder and comorbid ASD, and 4 additional variants showing ASD associations. At least 12 autism-associated variations in other genes impact CaMK4 signaling pathways, and 3 environmental risk factors affecting CaMK4 signaling have been identified in preclinical ASD models. CaMK4 is proposed as a convergence point in a common autism pathogenesis network.

biological.citation: Impaired CAMK4 Activity Limits Atherosclerosis and Reprograms Myelopoiesis (PMID: 40336480)
biological.summary: RNA sequencing revealed increased CaMK4 expression in advanced/unstable human carotid artery plaque, validated in both mouse and human atherosclerotic lesions with CaMK4 enriched in plaque macrophages. Camk4-/- hypercholesterolemic mice developed smaller, more stable lesions and showed peripheral monocytosis skewed toward non-classical Ly6clow monocytes. Mechanistically, CaMK4 loss promoted ATF6-mediated transcriptional regulation and increased Nr4a1 expression, driving a proreparative myeloid phenotype.

biological.citation: ASHG 2016 - Rare variants in 5α-reductase-2 and GWAS susceptibility loci are associated with elevated androgen levels in polycystic ovary syndrome (M. Dapas et al.)
biological.summary: Whole genome sequencing of 64 two-generation PCOS families identified a significant association between rare variants in CAMK4 and elevated testosterone levels in women with polycystic ovary syndrome. The association with testosterone was genome-wide significant after correction for multiple testing. This implicates CAMK4 rare variants in androgen dysregulation in PCOS.
